applicabilityBasis.summary: Falcon Digital Limited's USDf Terms permit USDf-funded card payments and redemption for originally deposited digital collateral or other stablecoins. GENIUS section 2(22) separately requires an issuer obligation to redeem for fixed monetary value and defines exclusions. Under owner ruling D17, crypto collateral, U.S. access restrictions and the separate fUSD product do not establish a USDf exemption. Applicability remains unclear pending qualified token-specific holder-contract analysis; authorization research is separate.

genius.notes: The prior 2026-06-07 editorial non-payment-token classification is withdrawn on 2026-10-01 under D17 pending qualified USDf-specific legal analysis. Current Terms expressly support USDf card payments, while direct redemption returns digital collateral or other stablecoins; neither fact alone resolves the statutory monetary-value obligation. U.S. access restrictions and the distinct Anchorage-issued fUSD product do not establish a USDf exclusion or authorization. Historical reserve-report observations are retained: the quarterly HT Digital report covers 2026-04-30 and is signed 2026-06-19; weekly collateral letters do not establish monthly formal assurance. The public app guide expressly describes 1:1 stablecoin redemption after cooldown, supporting the redemption-policy presence flag but not resolving whether USDf holders have the statutory national-currency/deposit redemption obligation. Falcon's July 2025 roadmap described group-level regulatory discussions and licensing ambitions under GENIUS/CLARITY and MiCA; no current USDf-specific filed application, permitted-issuer approval, foreign registration or committed issuer pathway was found. The May 2026 fUSD launch names Anchorage Digital Bank N.A. as that distinct token's issuer. No authorization is inherited by USDf. Negative research is bounded to opened public materials and exact-name official-domain searches, not a comprehensive regulator certification. The Act remains pre-effective on the reviewed landscape; section 3(b)'s broad DASP restriction has its separate July 18, 2028 start date. No public token-specific enforcement action was found in this review.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No opened public record or exact-name official-domain search established USDf/Falcon Digital Limited GENIUS permitted-issuer approval, state qualification, token-specific filed application or registered foreign exception. The public OCC table is a digital-assets bank application table, not a complete PPSI registry. General Falcon licensing ambitions do not identify a current USDf route; Anchorage issuance evidence relates to fUSD only. No token-specific public enforcement action was found. Absence is not a legal finding of non-compliance.
